time.desc: The country’s leader publicly criticized the country’s highest judicial body’s ruling on the legal basis for tariffs on social platforms and declared that he would continue to impose taxes through alternative routes.
The country holds talks with allied officials on the future of an existing trade agreement

The country signed an executive order to set extremely high tariffs on imported patented brand-name drugs, and required local production or participation in pricing arrangements as conditions for exemptions.

The executive order imposing 100% tariff on imported brand-name drugs stipulates that patented drugs that are not produced in Country Y and are not included in the drug pricing agreement will face full tariffs, which can be reduced to 20% if they are transferred to Country Y. Large pharmaceutical companies will receive a 120-day buffer, and small companies will receive a 180-day grace. Those who have signed a most-favored-nation pricing agreement with Institution C2 and local producers will be exempted; Country Y Such agreements have been reached with 17 pharmaceutical manufacturers (13 finalized, 4 under negotiation)

In the tariff arrangement for brand-name drugs, drugs produced by Regional Organization A, Country G, Country I and Country E1 enjoy a 15% preferential tariff due to existing trade agreements, and Country E has separate arrangements; generic drugs are exempted for at least one year, and orphan drugs, veterinary drugs and special drugs from trade agreement countries or that meet urgent public health needs are also exempted
The country adjusted its tariff rules on metals and their derivatives under the name of national security, expanded exemptions and lowered tax rates on some equipment to simplify implementation.

The adjusted national security tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper stipulate that derivatives with a metal content of less than 15% are exempt from 50% tariffs, and tariffs on some metal-intensive industrial and power grid equipment are reduced from 50% to 15% (valid until 2027). Derivatives with a content exceeding 15% are subject to a 25% unified tariff. All metal-produced products using Country Y but manufactured overseas are subject to a 10% lower tariff. The 50% tariff on raw materials remains unchanged but is calculated based on the sales price; senior officials said it aims to simplify the previously overly complex tariff system.

Public opinion narratives emerged in Chinese social media and financial discussions about Leader A resuming a certain 50% additional tariff and re-escalating the previously suspended tariff war; GT only serves as a record of public opinion on that day, and does not identify specific applicable countries, implementation details or market statements as policy facts that have been confirmed by many parties.

Country G The Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a new version of the Diplomatic Blue Book, which downgraded the Country X - Country G relationship from one of the most important bilateral relations to important neighboring countries for the first time, and included for the first time an analysis of the impact of Leader A reciprocal tariffs on Country G - Country Y economic relations; the Blue Book not only emphasizes the importance of Country Y maintaining Indo-Pacific commitments, but also acknowledges that tariff policies have brought pressure to Country G - Country Y economic and trade relations.

Country X Institution K2 responded to the Country G Diplomatic Blue Book, pointing the source of the deterioration of relations between Country X - Country G to Country G's Taiwan-related remarks by the Prime Minister that challenged the red line of the post-war international order, and requiring the Country G side to withdraw its wrong remarks

The country's leader threatened to impose "up to the maximum additional tariffs" on its major trading partners on the grounds of a regional security crisis. The other party officially denied the accusation and opposed unilateral pressure.

The country's customs is advancing the tax refund system and importer registration that have been judicially denied tariffs, while the government is using other legal tools to maintain the global tariff increase framework.
